name: Hushai
title: David's Friend and Advisor
summary: Hushai (also known as Husham) was an Arkite and a close friend and advisor to King David. He played a crucial role during Absalom's rebellion by infiltrating Absalom's court and countering Ahithophel's advice, which gave David time to flee and reorganize his forces.

keyEvents.title: David's Friend and Advisor
keyEvents.description: Hushai was known as David's friend, a trusted advisor at the court. He became one of David's closest confidants.

keyEvents.title: The Meeting with David on the Mount of Olives
keyEvents.description: When David fled from Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion, Hushai met him on the Mount of Olives with torn clothes and dust on his head as a sign of mourning. David asked him to return to work against Ahithophel's advice.

keyEvents.title: Hushai Wins Absalom's Trust
keyEvents.description: Hushai went to Absalom and declared his loyalty to him. Absalom accepted him, and Hushai thus gained access to Absalom's inner circle.

keyEvents.title: Hushai Counters Ahithophel's Advice
keyEvents.description: When Ahithophel advised Absalom to pursue David immediately, Hushai gave opposite counsel and recommended gathering a larger army first. Absalom chose to follow Hushai's advice, which gave David valuable time.

keyEvents.title: Hushai Sends Warning to David
keyEvents.description: After the council meeting, Hushai sent a message through the priests Zadok and Abiathar and their sons Jonathan and Ahimaaz, so that David was warned to cross the Jordan immediately.

keyEvents.title: Ahithophel's Suicide as a Result of Hushai's Victory
keyEvents.description: When Ahithophel saw that his advice was not followed, he realized that Absalom's cause was lost. He went home, settled his affairs, and took his own life. Thus, Hushai's intervention changed the course of the war.
